signals.name: allocRequestedBytes
signals.quantity: bytes the NEWARRAY int instruction in IntBlockBuilder.<init> is asked to allocate, computed as (long)initialSize * Integer.BYTES using long arithmetic to avoid the very overflow that is the vulnerability
signals.reset: AllocCounter.reset() called in V1Guidance.getInput() before returning the input stream

plans.retention: Primary: retain inputs whose allocRequestedBytes exceeds the current corpus maximum (hill-climb). Secondary: when allocRequestedBytes is zero or does not improve, retain 10% of inputs randomly to maintain exploration diversity and escape the breaker-trips trough (estimatedSize ~153M-536M). Corpus capped at 100 entries; on overflow, replace the lowest-signal entry. Prioritize parents for mutation proportionally to signal + 1.
mutation: byte-level: random byte flip at random position in the 8-byte input
byte-level: random byte overwrite at random position
byte-level: arithmetic increment/decrement on a random 4-byte field (big-endian int add/subtract random delta 1..256)
byte-level: replace one 4-byte field (bytes 0-3 or bytes 4-7) with a random int value
repetition ([R45a]): copy bytes 4-7 (estimatedSize) to bytes 0-3 (numAppends) or vice versa; for longer inputs double a random chunk

dictionary ([R45b]): overwrite a random 4-byte-aligned position with a token from {0x00000002 (literal 2 from Math.max), 0x00000004 (Integer.BYTES), 0x00000010 (NUM_BYTES_ARRAY_HEADER=16), 0x7FFFFFFF (Integer.MAX_VALUE), 0x00000000 (zero)}
no encoder needed ([R45c]): input is raw big-endian ints, no compression or checksum
